content.text: The cause is in the shell, not in room-14. `shell.mjs` line 27 fills the whole main-block interior with air, and `runParts` counts every cell an earlier part set (air included) as owned. Every master-bedroom cell lies inside that fill, so no room part can place anything. I'll remove room-14's writes as the brief asks and leave the layout data in place for when the shell is fixed.

input.summary:
parts/room-14.mjs (master bedroom) now runs clean: 0 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette, and make.sh writes build.nbt.
The part is empty, not furnished: the shell's air fill over the main block's interior owns every cell of this room, so all 84 writes were refused.
Layout data is kept in the file, and the calls to restore are written in its comment.

waste.what: Worked out why every write was refused by reading runParts and then shell.mjs. The REFUSED line names only the first 8 cells and never names the earlier part that owns them, so the cause was found by hand.
waste.cost: about 6 file reads and a manual count of the 84 writes (72 floor cells, 3 row-12/13 cells, 2 bed cells, 6 lantern cells) to confirm nothing else was refused
waste.tool: A runParts refusal line that names the owning part (e.g. 'owned by: mansion shell') and lists all refused cells, not 8. Or an `mcd parts --explain <part>` dry run that reports, per write, whether it lands on air the shell owns, before the build runs.

waste.what: Confirmed by hand that every master-bedroom write falls inside the shell's air fill (x27..68, y3..17, z43..60), so no move within the room was possible.
waste.cost: one grep and one sed over shell.mjs
waste.tool: A shell-level 'interior air is claimed' warning from runParts for any part whose box is wholly inside an earlier air fill; it would show the root cause on the first run.

companions.task: Change the shell's box() in parts/shell.mjs so the interior stays unowned: fill only the walls and floors, or leave the room air for the room parts. Then room-14 can restore its layout.
Place the bed, the dresser, the stair chairs and the table, and hang the lanterns from the restored room-14 calls, checking the bed halves and the chair facings after the shell is fixed.

left: The master bedroom is empty. Restoring its furniture needs parts/shell.mjs, line 27, changed so the air fill over the interior does not own the room cells (not mine to edit). Then restore the calls listed in room-14's comment.
room-14's LEGEND, FLOOR, Y12, Y13 and the imports of layers, bed and porchLantern are now unused. They are kept on purpose for the restore.

Out of scope: roof.json (or the roof spec) makes off-palette blocks (tuff_brick_slab, cobbled_deepslate_stairs, polished_deepslate_slab and others, 2178 placed). It shows in make.sh's output but is not from this part.
